# Command Reference

Every command of `scripts/playbook.py`, rendered from the engine's own argument parser and fact-sheet schemas. Common flags on every command: `--format brief|json` (default brief), `--lang he|en` (default he), `--unsealed`.

Exit codes: 0 ok, 1 the draft or talk track needs work, 2 bad input, 3 the integrity seal is broken.

In this file: interview | lint | template | send-time | cadence | decode | prep | guard | scene | debrief | intro | bench | schema | doctor.

## interview

What to ask the founder next, the picture so far, and the fact sheets for the other commands.

```text
playbook.py interview [-h] [--in INFILE] [--json JSON]
```

Fact sheet fields (unknown fields are rejected):

```text
mode: email | decode | prep | scene | intro (required)
    What the founder came for: email, decode (a meeting or thread), prep, scene (a simulation) or intro.
answers: object
    What the founder has said so far, keyed by question id. Each question printed by this command says how to record its answer. null means: there is none.
skipped: list of str
    Ids of questions the founder could not or would not answer. They are not asked again.
depth: quick | standard | deep
    quick = musts only, standard = musts and what sharpens, deep = the whole bank for this situation.
stop: bool
    True when the founder says enough. The commands run with what there is, and the gaps are named.
today: YYYY-MM-DD
    Today's date on the founder's calendar. Passed on to the fact sheets.
```

Example:

```json
{
  "mode": "decode",
  "today": "2026-11-24",
  "answers": {
    "context": "sales",
    "quotes": [
      "This is amazing! Let's keep in touch."
    ],
    "next_step_exists": false
  }
}
```

## lint

Measure an English email draft against the playbook rules.

```text
playbook.py lint [-h] [--type {breakup,cold,conference,followup,intro,investor_update,linkedin,recap,reply,scheduling,thank_you}] [--file FILE] [--source SOURCE]
```

Types: `breakup`, `cold`, `conference`, `followup`, `intro`, `investor_update`, `linkedin`, `recap`, `reply`, `scheduling`, `thank_you`.

## template

Render one of the playbook's email templates; unfilled slots stay as [brackets].

```text
playbook.py template [-h] [--id ID] [--list] [--set SLOT=VALUE] [--tz TZ] [--now NOW]
```

Templates: `cold`, `conference`, `forwardable`, `recap`, `value_bump`, `second_angle`, `breakup`, `re_entry`, `investor_update`, `bar_extraction`, `thank_you`, `loop_close`, `linkedin`, `scheduling`, `intro_reply_bcc`.

## send-time

The next send moments in the recipient's morning window, on both clocks.

```text
playbook.py send-time [-h] --tz TZ [--now NOW] [--count COUNT]
```

Zones: AKT, AZ, CT, ET, HT, MT, PT, any IANA name for those zones, or a major US city.

## cadence

The five follow-up touches after a meeting, with dates on both clocks.

```text
playbook.py cadence [-h] --meeting-date MEETING_DATE [--tz TZ] [--today TODAY] [--sent SENT] [--ics PATH]
```

## decode

Decode what an American said and return the traffic-light verdict and the next move.

```text
playbook.py decode [-h] [--in INFILE] [--json JSON] [--force]
```

Fact sheet fields (unknown fields are rejected):

```text
context: sales | investor | kol (required)
    Who the American is: sales (customer or partner), investor, or kol (domain expert).
today: YYYY-MM-DD
    Today's date on the founder's calendar. Defaults to the system date in Israel.
meeting_date: YYYY-MM-DD
    Date of the meeting or of the last live interaction.
source: recall | transcript | email_thread
    recall = the founder is telling the story; transcript or email_thread = their exact words are in front of you.
quotes: list of str
    What the American said, word for word. Never a paraphrase.
next_step: object
    The next step, if one exists.
  exists: bool (required)
      Is there any agreed next step?
  date: YYYY-MM-DD
      Its calendar date. No date means no dated step.
  proposed_by: them | founder | nobody
      Who proposed it.
  accepted_by_them: bool
      True when it is on THEIR calendar or they confirmed it in writing.
  what: str
      What the step is.
cost_to_them: list of objects
    What this has cost THEM so far. An empty list means: nothing yet.
  currency: calendar_time | data_access | intro | signature | money (required)
  evidence: str (required)
      The concrete thing: a date, a name, a file.
signals: list of objects
    Signals the founder reports. Each needs evidence or it does not count. Run `schema decode` for the ids.
  id: str (required)
  evidence: str
their_questions: int
    How many real questions they asked.
touches_sent: int
    Follow-ups sent since their last reply, all unanswered.
touches_done: list of (recap | value | second_angle | breakup | nurture)
    Cadence touches already sent.
last_reply_date: YYYY-MM-DD
    Date of their last reply.
reply_latency_days: number
    Their typical reply time, in days.
tz: str
    Recipient timezone or city, for the send date of the next move.
decision_needed: str
    The decision the founder needs from this debrief.
flags: list of (pricing_raised_without_model | strategic_fork | founder_resists_verdict)
    Coaching context flags.
bench_used: int
    Bench nudges already used in this session.
```

Signal ids (each needs evidence to count):

```text
sales/green: added_people, reference_call_request, asked_pricing, asked_security, asked_integration, next_meeting_booked_in_meeting, fast_replies
sales/yellow: compliments_no_step, circle_back, loop_in_unnamed
sales/red: ghosting, keep_posted_no_questions, refuses_concrete_step, reach_out_anytime
investor/green: second_meeting_scheduled_in_meeting, more_partners_joining, data_room_request, reference_request, cohort_request, unprompted_terms_talk, intro_to_portfolio_or_fund, open_diligence_request
investor/yellow: warm_replies_no_date, stuck_at_associate, circle_back, loop_in_unnamed
investor/red: questions_stopped_only_compliments, rescheduled_without_alternatives, ghosting, keep_posted_no_questions, reach_out_anytime
kol/green: criticism_voiced, behavior_data_shared, named_who_should_not_buy
```

Example:

```json
{
  "context": "sales",
  "today": "2026-11-24",
  "meeting_date": "2026-11-17",
  "quotes": [
    "This is amazing!",
    "Let's keep in touch."
  ],
  "next_step": {
    "exists": false
  },
  "cost_to_them": [],
  "their_questions": 0,
  "tz": "ET"
}
```

## prep

Build the prep sheet for a sales, investor or KOL meeting.

```text
playbook.py prep [-h] [--in INFILE] [--json JSON]
```

Fact sheet fields (unknown fields are rejected):

```text
type: sales | investor | kol
    sales (customer or partner), investor, or kol (domain expert). Mandatory: it decides the framework.
goal_currency: calendar_time | data_access | intro | signature | money
    What the founder wants to walk out with.
goal: str
    The goal in the founder's words.
the_ask: str
    The one ask the founder will make before the meeting ends.
city: str
    Where the American is based.
region: new_york | west_coast | midwest_south | other
    Overrides the region guessed from the city.
tz: str
    Recipient timezone, when the city does not settle it.
meeting_minutes: int
meeting_date: YYYY-MM-DD
today: YYYY-MM-DD
counterpart: object
  name: str
  role: str
  org: str
meeting_number: int
    1 for a first meeting.
live_thread: bool
    True when a fundraise is actively running.
background: str
    Relationship history, in the founder's words.
bench_used: int
```

Example:

```json
{
  "type": "investor",
  "goal_currency": "calendar_time",
  "goal": "a second meeting with a second partner",
  "the_ask": "What would you need to see for this to be a strong yes?",
  "city": "New York",
  "meeting_minutes": 30,
  "meeting_date": "2026-12-02",
  "counterpart": {
    "name": "Jennifer",
    "role": "Partner",
    "org": "a US seed fund"
  }
}
```

## debrief

Score the founder's side of a simulation transcript.

```text
playbook.py debrief [-h] [--in INFILE] [--json JSON]
```

Fact sheet fields (unknown fields are rejected):

```text
type: sales | investor | kol (required)
injected: list of str
    Row ids from the scene card. Omit and pass seed instead to recompute them.
seed: str
    The seed printed on the scene card.
turns: list of objects (required)
    The transcript, in order.
  who: founder | american (required)
  text: str (required)
outcome: object
    How the conversation ended, as the American character saw it.
  result: dated_step | clean_no | vague (required)
bench_used: int
```

Example:

```json
{
  "type": "sales",
  "seed": "2026-11-24",
  "turns": [
    {
      "who": "american",
      "text": "This is really interesting!"
    },
    {
      "who": "founder",
      "text": "Thanks. Would Tuesday or Thursday work for a 20-minute follow-up with your data lead?"
    },
    {
      "who": "american",
      "text": "Send me a deck and I'll take a look."
    },
    {
      "who": "founder",
      "text": "Happy to send a one-pager today. Would Thursday at 10am work to walk through it?"
    }
  ],
  "outcome": {
    "result": "dated_step"
  }
}
```

## intro

Check a warm intro against the intro protocol.

```text
playbook.py intro [-h] [--in INFILE] [--json JSON]
```

Fact sheet fields (unknown fields are rejected):

```text
stage: asking | received | after_meeting | connecting (required)
    asking = requesting an intro; received = an intro landed; after_meeting = the meeting happened; connecting = you want to connect two others.
connector: str
    First name of the person who made or will make the intro.
forwardable_attached: bool
    asking: is a forwardable email attached?
gave_before: bool
    asking: have you done something for this connector before?
hours_since_intro: number
    received: hours since the intro email arrived.
replied: bool
    received: did you already reply?
moved_to_bcc: bool
    received: did your first reply move the connector to BCC?
hours_since_meeting: number
    after_meeting: hours since the meeting.
loop_closed: bool
    after_meeting: did you tell the connector what happened?
both_agreed: bool
    connecting: did both people agree to be connected?
```

Example:

```json
{
  "stage": "received",
  "connector": "Sarah",
  "hours_since_intro": 30,
  "replied": false
}
```
